title: How to Persuade Senior Leaders at Work
summary: This video explains a research-backed story framework to help professionals persuade senior leaders and get a "yes" on proposals, budgets, or extra time. The creator breaks down common mistakes like overcomplicating, rambling, and poor structure, and provides a 5-step presentation framework based on human psychology.
key_points: To be persuasive to senior leaders, focus on four things: clarity, relevance, business value, and low perceived risk.
Mistake 1: Explain WHY it matters before HOW it works. Address the business value first.
Mistake 2: Stop using overly complex jargon and corporate blah-blah. Explain terms or use simple language everyone understands.
Mistake 3: Do not make pre-read slides identical to the presentation slides. Keep pre-read slides to the main message and use the meeting for dialogue.
Mistake 4: Avoid poor structure and rambling. Use a clear structure based on human psychology.
Loss aversion: Humans experience losses two times more strongly than equivalent gains. Address risks and concerns in advance.
The 5-step presentation framework: 1. Start with a hook. 2. Explain pain or possibility. 3. Back it up with data (proof). 4. Explain the pay off. 5. End with a call to action.
